subject: ACME POC: integration plan, success criteria, and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acme.com>, Lena Ortiz <lena.ortiz@acme.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: ACME POC: integration plan, success criteria, and next steps

Hi Samir / Lena —

Thanks again for a productive discovery call today. To capture what we discussed and keep momentum on the POC, below is a proposed evaluation plan, success criteria, owners, and an initial integration checklist. Please read through and let me know any corrections. If this looks good I recommend we lock the week of July 27 for a short kickoff + technical deep dive.

High-level POC objective:
- Validate Redwood inference for in-product question-answering and content summarization across your customer support KB with acceptable latency (< 300ms median) and per-token cost under your internal target.

Success criteria (what ACME needs to see):
1) Functional: generate accurate answers on a representative prompt set (70%+ answer precision on your annotated eval set).
2) Performance: median latency <= 300ms at your target concurrency (10 qps), 95th percentile under 800ms.
3) Cost: per-1000-tokens cost within forecasted budget (we will run cost sims during POC).
4) Operational: observed stable stream responses and tool-calling integration for lookup enrichment.

Proposed evaluation plan & timeline:
- Week 0 (by Jul 21): share integration docs + seed test vectors and annotated eval set (ACME).
- Week 1 (Jul 27 kickoff): integration work — SDK quickstart, auth, sample routes.
- Week 2 (Aug 3): run initial batch evals and latency load tests.
- Week 3 (Aug 10): tune batching/quantization profiles, validate tool-calling flow.
- Week 4 (Aug 17): final eval, review results, decide next steps.

Ownership:
- ACME: provide eval set, sample traffic pattern, and test account. (Samir / Lena)
- Redwood: integration support, SE time for SDK + streaming setup (Dylan), POC monitoring + evals (Marissa).

Initial integration checklist (technical highlights) — Dylan, please see notes and confirm feasibility:
- SDK: use Redwood Node/Python SDK (v0.9+) for quickstart.
- API routes: tokenized generation (POST /v1/generate), streaming via server-sent events or websockets for UI.
- Tool calling: recommend using Redwood's structured tool calling JSON to enrich responses with DB lookups; falls back to model when tool returns empty.
- Auth: API key initially, then mTLS or VPC private endpoints for Dedicated if required.
- Observability: we will enable per-request tracing and token-level cost breakdowns for POC.

Attachments: redwood-integration-guide.pdf (quickstart + sample code), ACME annotated eval set request form.

Next steps (action items):
- Samir/Lena: confirm eval set delivery date and whether you want streaming or polling in your UI prototype.
- Dylan (cc'd): confirm SDK versions and any blockers on tool calling flow.
- I will schedule the Jul 27 kickoff once you confirm availability.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this started.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

Hi Samir / Lena —

Thanks — happy to take point on the integration side. Quick technical answers and a proposed implementation plan below.

SDK and quickstart:
- Use Redwood Node SDK v0.9.2 or Python SDK v0.9.4 — both support streaming and structured tool calling. Sample install: npm i @redwood/inference@0.9.2 or pip install redwood-inference==0.9.4.
- Quick code snippet for streaming (Node):
  const stream = client.generateStream({ model: 'redwood-chat-1', input: prompt });
  stream.on('data', chunk => ui.append(chunk.text));

API routes and auth:
- POST /v1/generate: synchronous generation (non-streaming).
- /v1/stream: SSE-compatible endpoint for progressive tokens; websocket support available for high-throughput UIs.
- Tool calling flow: POST /v1/tool/invoke with structured payload { tool_name, args } — tool returns JSON which the model can reference. (We will provide an adapter sample and retry/backoff guidance.)

Latency considerations and batching:
- For your target concurrency (10 qps) we recommend enabling small dynamic batching with max_batch_size=8 and a batch_timeout_ms=15. This typically keeps median latency low while improving throughput.
- KV cache warmup: first-token latency will be higher; we suggest warmup traffic before timed latency tests.

Observability & eval hooks:
- We'll enable per-request traces and token cost breakdowns in the POC workspace. Exported logs and a shared dashboard will be created.

Owners and timeline (confirming Marissa's plan):
- By Jul 22: ACME provides eval set (Samir).
- Jul 27 (kickoff): SE deep dive, provisioning of POC API key and test workspace (Dylan).
- Aug 3: run initial batch evals (Dylan + Marissa).
- Aug 10: tuning and tool-calling validation (Dylan).
- Aug 17: final review (Marissa / Samir).

Attachments: poc-integration-checklist.xlsx (checklist with implementation tasks and owner columns).

Open questions for ACME:
- Do you need us to host a temporary webhook endpoint for tool-calling testing, or will you provide a reachable dev endpoint behind a tunnel?
- Any IP allowlist restrictions for the test workspace?

I can prep the SDK sample repo and a runnable demo for the kickoff. Marissa — I put Rishi on CC for procurement timelines.

Thanks,
Dylan
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
dylan.brooks@redwood.ai
